To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

A log, spreadsheet, database export, or other record showing the total number of open-government mediation complaints/requests received by the Attorney General's office for each of the past five calendar years (2021–2026 to date, or by fiscal year if that is how the office tracks them).
For each complaint in that period, the disposition or current status (e.g., resolved/settled, closed due to impasse, referred to litigation, withdrawn, pending), to the extent this is tracked in any existing record. If dispositions are not tracked per-complaint, please provide aggregate counts by disposition category.
Any record(s) supporting or underlying the statement that the office "has handled roughly 480 open-government complaints this year," including how "open-government complaint" is defined or counted for that figure, and whether that figure includes Open Meetings Act complaints, Open Records Act complaints, or both.
Any policy, procedure, or internal guidance document describing when the mediation program closes a complaint as an "impasse" versus continuing to pursue it, and when (if ever) the office refers a matter for its own independent civil enforcement action under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-73 rather than closing it.

If any of the above is maintained in an electronic database or case-management system, I request production in its native electronic/exportable format (e.g., CSV or Excel) rather than as a PDF or printout. If the office asserts any exemption as to part of a record, I request that the remainder be produced with the exempt portion redacted, per O.C.G.A. § 50-18-72(g).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

title: LVMPD data sharing with LexisNexis or SoundThinking

communications.subject: Nevada Public Records Act Request: LVMPD data sharing with LexisNexis or SoundThinking
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting the following records:

1. Any contract, subscription agreement, order form, renewal or amendment between the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department (LVMPD) and LexisNexis Risk Solutions for Accurint for Law Enforcement or the Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC), including any addendum that allows LVMPD records to be shared through LexisNexis (sometimes called a data contribution addendum, or "AVCC XML Addendum").

2. Any contract, subscription agreement, or data-sharing agreement between LVMPD and SoundThinking, Inc. (formerly Forensic Logic) for CrimeTracer or CopLinkX, including any terms that allow LVMPD records to be searched by other agencies through CrimeTracer.

3. The records described in items 1 and 2 held by LVMPD in its role as fiscal agent for the Nevada High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (Nevada HIDTA), including agreements covering accounts used by Nevada HIDTA staff, task forces or initiatives.

4. Invoices or purchase orders for the services in items 1 through 3, including any paid with Nevada HIDTA grant funds.

I am researching how Nevada law enforcement agencies share records through commercial data platforms. A Nevada HIDTA intelligence analyst job posting lists Accurint as a tool used in the role. Many Accurint users also choose to share local RMS/CAD/CFS/JMS records with LexisNexis - our goal is to determine if LVMPD shares local records with LexisNexis or CrimeTracer as part of their data sharing programs. 

Time range: January 1, 2020 through the date of fulfillment. Please send electronic copies by email or cloud link.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal
